text:
Situation: Sterile water from Nephron SC, LLC (FEI 3010892830) has been on FDA's shortage list since 2021-11-23. As of 2026-10-21 the shortage has lasted 59 months. Corvale East has 2.7 days on hand (95 units); Corvale General has 8.3 days on hand (293.55 units). An approved therapeutic interchange to WATER 1 mL/mL from Hospira, Inc. (NDC 00409488710) was authorized by Riley Brooks, PharmD on 2026-05-18.

Why (FDA record): FDA inspected the Nephron plant in 2011 (OAI, known 2011-09-15), 2014 (OAI, 18 observations, known 2014-05-22), and 2015 (OAI, known 2015-11-12). Warning Letters were issued 2013-09-24 and 2016-09-02. A 2019 inspection ended 2019-11-15 and was classified VAI (letter dated 2022-04-13, 739 days before shortage posting). A Warning Letter was issued 2020-09-22 (427 days before shortage posting). An inspection ending 2022-04-20 was classified OAI with 6 observations citing validation lacking for sterile drug products (148 days after shortage posting). Warning Letters followed on 2022-10-11 and 2022-10-21 (322 and 332 days after shortage posting). Class II recalls for sterile water from this firm started 2023-01-12 and 2023-02-23 (415 and 457 days after shortage posting). A 2023-02-10 inspection was classified OAI with 15 observations citing SOPs not followed and validation lacking (444 days after shortage posting). Inspections in 2024-02-09 and 2024-09-25 were also OAI. The most recent inspection ended 2025-08-22 and was classified VAI.

Our position: Current inventory is critically low at Corvale East and marginal at Corvale General. The Hospira alternate is approved and clinically equivalent. Other potential suppliers are not on FDA's shortage list but their labels do not identify a verifiable manufacturing plant.

Recommended actions:
1. Activate the Hospira therapeutic interchange for all sterile water orders — requires approval by Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee.
2. Place immediate purchase orders for Hospira NDC 00409488710 to replenish both sites — requires approval by Pharmacy Director.
3. Evaluate Chartwell RX, LLC and HealthFirst (HF Acquisition Co LLC) as backup sources only after plant verification — requires approval by Buyer and Quality Assurance.
4. Monitor FDA shortage list daily and report supply status weekly to the committee — requires approval by Pharmacy Manager.

Not recommended: Switching to any alternate supplier whose manufacturing site cannot be verified; delaying the Hospira interchange pending further review; increasing par levels without confirmed supply.
